kept.heading: BRANDED SEARCH IS BECOMING A LESS RELIABLE PROXY FOR BRAND DEMAND (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Branded search has long been a proxy for brand demand, but it's becoming less reliable. Data shows branded queries dropping even as demand holds steady, pointing to a measurement gap, not a demand decline. AI search is shifting decisions upstream, answering questions before users search for brands. The risk is misreading weaker search as weaker brands and underinvesting in brand building. Branded search still matters, but it should be one signal, not the source of truth.

kept.heading: DOES TOPICAL AUTHORITY MATTER IN AI SEARCH? (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Topical authority still matters in AI search, with data from Semrush's analysis of 50,000+ brands showing AI answers develop category owners over time. In ChatGPT's June 2026 data, only 15.2% of categories had a clear owner, leaving 89.3% of AI search demand in categories without one. Category owners also showed stronger brand search volume, organic traffic, and authority. Build depth in core topics rather than chase broad content coverage.

kept.heading: WHAT EVERYONE GETS WRONG ABOUT CATEGORY CREATION (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Category creation only works when it reflects a real job to be done instead of a new marketing label. Companies create confusion when they invent platform names that don't match a clear customer responsibility or workflow. It's better to create a new job to be done before naming a category, sell products as a suite when buyers purchase them separately, or lead with the product the market already understands and expand from there.

kept.heading: THOUGHTLESS FEATURES NEVER ADD UP TO A THOUGHTFUL PRODUCT (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Teams ship “ham biscuit” features fast, solving surface problems but missing real user needs. Idea generators stay detached, copying competitors or AI outputs, while execution follows without question. The result is bloated products that hurt clarity and sales. Better products come from defining real workflows, not stacking features. Focus on the job to be done, validate outcomes, and design end-to-end experiences instead of isolated fixes.

kept.heading: SUBJECTLINE.COM (TOOL)
kept.blurb: This is a free email subject line tester that scores over 15M subject lines and helps improve email performance. Free accounts provide subject line history, score tracking, and AI-powered rewrites. Pro accounts ($9.99/year) add open rate predictions, industry benchmarks, and project organization tools.

kept.heading: RCS OR SMS? IT DEPENDS ON THE TASK (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: RCS now reaches 96% of US devices and offers rich media, interactivity, and branding, but costs at least twice as much as SMS. Like HTML email, it adds capability, not necessity. Use RCS when visuals or actions help complete a task like browsing products or resolving issues. Stick with SMS for simple, urgent updates like order confirmations or codes.

kept.heading: AI IS WORKING OVERTIME. SO AM I (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI users save an average of 5.1 hours a week but lose 3.3 hours learning or troubleshooting the same tools. 77% report a heavier workload, while 23% report AI-related anxiety. The shortfall comes from generation time being mistaken for completion time, since a report that takes one minute to draft still needs its research checked and its logic fixed before it is usable. The technology accelerates the first draft while leaving the harder work, review and accountability, exactly where it was.

kept.heading: THE BIGGEST TECHNICAL SEO TIME-WASTERS TO AVOID (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Chasing minor SEO fixes like redirects, crawl budget, 404s, or tool flags wastes time when they don't impact rankings or user experience.

kept.heading: MY GOAL IS TO NEVER APPLY FOR A MARKETING JOB EVER AGAIN (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Build a personal brand before you need it by staying visible and optimizing LinkedIn.

kept.heading: TELL YOUR ENGINEER TO CHANGE "LOADING..." TO "THINKING..." (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Products that hide their "thinking" step read as less warm to users.

kept.heading: AI CONTENT IS EVERYWHERE ON SOCIAL MEDIA, ESPECIALLY LINKEDIN (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI-generated content is spreading across social media, with longform posts hit the hardest. Pangram data from over 1M posts shows 13.8% flagged as AI, rising to 25% for posts over 250 words. LinkedIn drives nearly two-thirds of flagged content, with over 40% of longform posts fully AI-generated. X shows the highest combined AI use when including mixed content. Reddit replies remain mostly human, but top-level posts show higher AI rates, revealing gaps in moderation.

kept.heading: OPENAI APPEARS TO BE MISSING ITS SALES GOALS BY A VAST MARGIN (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI's $100 billion ad-revenue target for 2030 requires three things to happen at once. Advertisers moving decades of search and social budgets into chatbots, OpenAI out-competing Google and Meta for that spend, and the entire AI ad market growing roughly 100 times from where it sits today. The category's entire addressable market currently tops out around $5.4B, and OpenAI itself is on pace to miss its own ad revenue forecast by about 90% this year.

kept.heading: COPYWRITING BREAKDOWN: HOW TO SELL SOMETHING ORDINARY (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Strong marketing often comes from better research instead of better copy. Claude Hopkins won customers in a crowded category by asking hundreds of consumers what they wanted, measuring how Palmolive performed against those needs, and turning the results into specific proof points. The ad replaced vague claims with numbers such as 250 times more lather, 15% water absorption in one minute, and lather that lasted 10 minutes. Research, measurable evidence, and clear messaging can make an ordinary product stand out even when competitors offer similar features.

kept.heading: SWAG THAT WORKS: THE NEW RULES FOR TRADE SHOW GIVEAWAYS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 47% of marketers already treat branded merchandise as a core marketing channel, and 87% of recipients keep and use what they receive rather than tossing it. Middesk built a tiered swag strategy around that shift at Money20/20, gating higher-value items behind booth actions like booking a sales meeting or agreeing to a case study, then generated 10 times its activation spend in new pipeline and 26 times more in influenced pipeline. The gifting also produced a surprise: a steep jump in LinkedIn followers driven entirely by pins and luggage tags that were never meant to be the campaign's main goal.

kept.heading: OPAL U: BECOME A CERTIFIED AI EXPERT IN 5 DAYS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Opal U is a free 5-day live cohort for senior marketers who need to prove AI ROI and move fast. Built for VPs and heads of marketing who feel stuck in the hype and need practical output. Spend one hour a day building three AI agents that automate real work and save 10+ hours a week.

kept.heading: HOW THE FOUNDER OF MORNING BREW BUILT A CLAUDE CONTENT MACHINE THAT NEVER RUNS OUT OF IDEAS (43 MINUTE VIDEO)
kept.blurb: Alex Lieberman's Content Machine scans seven days of Slack, Notion, Gmail, and meeting notes, plus the accounts he follows on X and LinkedIn, then ranks 15 content ideas a day so the blank page never becomes the bottleneck. Six AI personas modeled on interviewers like Tim Ferriss and Howard Stern question him until they extract real specifics, and his voice-to-texted answers trace every sentence back to something he actually said. Before anything posts, a six-persona Writer's Council scores the draft and blocks it from going below a 9 out of 10.

kept.heading: HOW MUCH CREATIVE DEBT ARE YOU CARRYING? (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Creative work needs recurring time on the calendar or it will always lose to urgent tasks. "Creative debt" is the cost of repeatedly delaying creative projects until avoiding them becomes part of your identity instead of a temporary choice. Treat creative projects like recurring commitments by scheduling dedicated time, reduce project scope, and keep momentum through small, consistent actions instead of waiting for the perfect moment. You should also remove pressure to prove ROI so creative work can exist without immediate business value. The goal is to stop delaying meaningful projects before postponement blocks future creative output.

kept.heading: WHY YOUR TOP KEYWORDS ARE QUIETLY LOSING VOLUME (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Head term queries are what fund Google's ad business, since two-word category terms draw 5x to 15x the CPC of longtail equivalents, and those same head terms are now shrinking in 7 of 9 consumer categories. Entertainment's head term volume fell 16% year over year, the sharpest decline in the dataset, in a category where AI tools already give users a credible substitute for a Google search entirely. The bigger risk for Google isn't cannibalized clicks on searches that still happen, it's users skipping the search box altogether for tools like ChatGPT on exactly the head term queries the ad auction depends on.

kept.heading: 10 CREATIVE WAYS TO WRITE WITH AI WITHOUT LOSING YOUR SOUL (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Tips on how Ahrefs uses AI to create content, plus the experiments they've been running.

kept.heading: HOW MICHELOB ULTRA AND LEO MESSI PREPARED FOR THE MOST UNPREDICTABLE MARKETING MOMENT OF THE WORLD CUP (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Michelob Ultra built its Messi tribute ad around 20 years of career accomplishments, letting the same creative work whether Argentina won or lost the final.

kept.heading: THE B2B BLOG IS COLLAPSING. THE COMPANIES REPLACING IT ARE BECOMING PUBLISHERS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The SEO blog playbook is losing ground as zero-click search rises and platform reach declines. Owned media replaces it, with brands building publications for a defined audience. This model drives distribution through shares, interviews, and syndication. It also turns content into pipeline. Early results show traction from niche audiences and growing AI referrals.

kept.heading: WHY SAVVY MEDIA BUYERS ARE BETTING ON MALL ADVERTISING (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Media buyers are increasingly turning to mall advertising because it delivers something scarce in a fragmented media landscape: physically present and highly attentive audiences rather than sheer digital reach. Malls have shifted from pure retail destinations into lifestyle hubs, drawing people in for fitness classes and healthcare appointments as often as for shopping. That inventory is now largely digitized, so buyers can target every screen within a set distance of a specific location and measure results through foot traffic, offsite visits, and spend data instead of modeled estimates.

kept.heading: FRENCH LAWMAKERS APPROVE A SWEEPING SOCIAL MEDIA BAN FOR CHILDREN UNDER 15 (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: France's ban arrives alongside a broader European push on kids and social media, with the EU's top official calling for limits and an EU advisory panel recommending zero access for children under 13 until platforms can prove their products are safe. Spain and the UK have each floated similar restrictions, and the European Commission is expected to propose EU-wide rules for its 27 member countries.

kept.heading: HOW TO BUILD CURIOSITY INTO HIGH-PERFORMING SOCIAL ADS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Attention gets a viewer to notice a social ad, but curiosity is what keeps them from scrolling away in the next few seconds. Platforms are increasingly built to reward the second half of that equation. Meta and TikTok's AI-driven delivery systems now optimize for watch time, saves and shares, and clicks that happen after the video ends. These are all signals a genuinely curious viewer produces without prompting. Building that gap into the creative means designing open loops, such as a surprising statement or an unresolved problem, then demonstrating a result instead of describing it.

kept.heading: WHEN AND HOW TO CALL CUSTOMERS BY NAME (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Using a customer's name can increase spending and satisfaction when it feels natural and personal. Customers spent 17.3% more on average and accepted upsell offers more than twice as often when employees used their name during the interaction instead of only during the sales pitch. Introduce employees by name first and train staff to use customer names sparingly because scripted or repetitive use reduces the effect. Avoid using customer names in private or sensitive situations because discomfort can reverse the benefit.

kept.heading: USE MY /NO-AI-SLOP SKILL TO REMOVE 20+ PATTERNS OF AI SLOP FROM YOUR WRITING (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The free /no-ai-slop AI skill removes more than 20 common AI writing patterns from emails, documents, and other content. It can also detect AI-generated writing by identifying those same patterns and listing what it finds. The skill targets habits such as generic openers, fake insights, vague analysis, and other repetitive phrasing that makes AI writing easy to spot. You can install the skill from its GitHub repository and use it in Codex, Claude Code, or other AI coding assistants.

kept.heading: AI VISIBILITY IS A TOPIC-LEVEL GAME: A STUDY OF 50,000 BRANDS IN CHATGPT (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A study of 50K brands found that winning one ChatGPT prompt does not mean owning a topic. Only 15% of categories had a clear leader, leaving most topics open for competitors. Traditional SEO metrics like traffic and authority scores only predicted winners about half the time. Brands that consistently appear across related questions build stronger AI visibility. Once a brand gains a wide lead, it becomes harder to overtake.

kept.heading: HOW TO KNOW YOU'RE READY FOR A FRACTIONAL CMO AND HOW TO BRIEF ONE WELL (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Most companies wait until something breaks before hiring a fractional CMO. Readiness isn't about size, it's about having a real strategy gap and a team that can execute. Common signals include weak positioning and looming inflection points like a fundraise or expansion. It's not a fit without product market fit or an execution layer. Bring clear problems, real data, and defined decision rights to get value quickly.

kept.heading: MEASUREMENT IS A BUSINESS ADVANTAGE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Better measurement creates a competitive advantage because it uncovers profitable channels, improves ad platform optimization, and helps teams make budget decisions with confidence. Click-based reporting often undervalues channels like podcasts, influencers, and sponsorships, so companies that combine attribution surveys and brand signals can find lower cost opportunities before competitors do. Better conversion data also helps Google and Meta optimize for higher quality customers instead of low value leads.

kept.heading: INSIDE GENERAL MILLS'S BRAND ARCHIVE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: General Mills's brand archive functions as both a lookup service and a forward-looking curation system, holding more than 10,000 records across 5,000 square feet that trace the company's 160-year history. Brand teams query it for context on products like Bisquick and Betty Crocker, while the three-person team also flags today's campaigns as candidates for tomorrow's collection. The volume and variety of modern marketing content, spanning far more channels than earlier decades, has made deciding what to keep the hardest ongoing call.

kept.heading: THE MOST VALUABLE THING APPLE BUILT IN THE 2000S WASN'T THE IPOD (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Apple treated iTunes as a customer acquisition tool because song sales supported iPod adoption and later removed friction for products like the App Store and Apple Pay.
